chunks: Ali (peace be upon him) from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:
When a man travels by sea for trade, he endangers his religion.

key_terms.رُكُوبِ الْبَحْرِ: traveling by sea / riding the sea
key_terms.يُغَرِّرُ: he endangers / he deceives himself into loss

ai.seo_question: Why does traveling by sea for trade endanger a Muslim's religion?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) highlights that the inherent uncertainties of maritime commerce—such as prolonged separation, perilous conditions, and the pragmatic necessity of swearing oaths to secure goods—can gradually erode one's religious commitment. This narration, found in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving *din* amidst worldly pursuits, warning that the ease of compromising principles for profit in such high-stakes environments poses a spiritual danger.
